nodes.description: Loss of eyebrow and eyelash (and sometimes scalp) hair as follicles become dysplastic.

evidence.reference_title: Trichodysplasia spinulosa--a newly described folliculocentric viral infection in an immunocompromised host.
evidence.snippet: an immunocompromised individual who presented with progressive alopecia, friable follicular spinous processes, and erythematous, indurated papules.

nodes.description: The hyperproliferating inner root sheath cells, overloaded with trichohyalin granules, distend and abnormally differentiate the hair follicle so that it extrudes a keratin spicule in place of a normal hair shaft, giving the characteristic follicular papules with protruding spines and the associated alopecia.
nodes.id: Dysplastic Follicle and Keratin Spicule Formation

evidence.reference_title: Recent developments in trichodysplasia spinulosa disease.
evidence.snippet: TS presents with distinct histological features including the presence of large eosinophilic, trichohyaline granules within hyperproliferating inner root sheath cells of the hair bulb.

evidence.reference_title: Discovery of a new human polyomavirus associated with trichodysplasia spinulosa in an immunocompromized patient.
evidence.snippet: Histologically, TS is characterized by distended and abnormally maturated hair follicles with high numbers of inner root sheath cells containing excessive amounts of trichohyalin

nodes.description: Folliculocentric papules extruding keratin spines (spicules), centred on the face (nose, eyebrows, ears).

evidence.snippet: Keratin spines (spicules), mainly in the center of the face, clinically characterize this disease.

nodes.description: Driven through the cell cycle by the two T-antigen branches, the infected inner root sheath cells proliferate to create the expanded, Ki-67-positive cell pool that supports viral DNA replication and populates the dysplastic follicle. This convergent proliferation is the rate-limiting central effector.

biological_processes: positive regulation of cell population proliferation

evidence.reference_title: Polyomavirus-associated Trichodysplasia spinulosa involves hyperproliferation, pRB phosphorylation and upregulation of p16 and p21.
evidence.snippet: These data are compatible with a scenario of TSPyV T-antigen-mediated cell cycle progression, potentially creating a pool of proliferating cells that enable viral DNA replication and drive papule and spicule formation.

evidence.reference_title: Recent developments in trichodysplasia spinulosa disease.
evidence.snippet: TS is characterized by uncontrolled inner root sheath cell proliferation and folliculocentric papular eruption that can progress to disfiguring leonine facies when left untreated.

nodes.description: The TSPyV large T antigen binds the retinoblastoma protein (pRB), releasing E2F and driving the infected inner root sheath cell into S phase. In patient lesions, large T antigen colocalizes with intense Ki-67 staining at the follicle margins.
nodes.id: Large T Antigen Inactivation of the Retinoblastoma Protein

biological_processes: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

evidence.reference_title: Functional Analysis of Trichodysplasia Spinulosa-Associated Polyomavirus-Encoded Large T Antigen.
evidence.snippet: Immunoprecipitation assays revealed that TSPyV LT bound to retinoblastoma 1, but not to p53 in transfected cells.

evidence.reference_title: Polyomavirus-associated Trichodysplasia spinulosa involves hyperproliferation, pRB phosphorylation and upregulation of p16 and p21.
evidence.snippet: Intense Ki-67 staining was detected especially in the margins of TS hair follicles, which colocalized with TSPyV LT-antigen detection.

nodes.description: Facial skin thickening producing a disfiguring leonine appearance in advanced untreated disease.

evidence.reference_title: Recent developments in trichodysplasia spinulosa disease.
evidence.snippet: folliculocentric papular eruption that can progress to disfiguring leonine facies when left untreated.

nodes.description: Immunosuppression (solid-organ transplantation, chemotherapy for leukaemia, JAK inhibitors) removes the cell-mediated control that normally keeps near-ubiquitous TSPyV latent, permitting productive infection. Disease follows either primary infection in a never-exposed host or reactivation.
nodes.id: Loss of Immune Control of TSPyV

evidence.snippet: In immunocompromised individuals, primary infection with trichodysplasia spinulosa-associated polyomavirus (TSPyV) can cause the very rare skin disease trichodysplasia spinulosa (TS).

nodes.description: The TSPyV middle T antigen engages protein phosphatase 2A and hyperactivates the MEK/ERK/MNK1 signalling cascade, a second pro-proliferative drive on the infected follicular cell.

evidence.reference_title: Dysregulation of the MEK/ERK/MNK1 signalling cascade by middle T antigen of the trichoydsplasia spinulosa polyomavirus.
evidence.snippet: We describe a novel mechanism of action for mT antigen that involves hyperactivation of MEK, ERK and MNK1.

nodes.description: Freed from immune control, TSPyV replicates to very high loads (about 10^5-10^6 genome copies per cell) in the inner root sheath keratinocytes of hair follicles, with capsid protein expression restricted to those cells.
nodes.id: Productive TSPyV Infection of Inner Root Sheath Keratinocytes

evidence.reference_title: Trichodysplasia spinulosa is characterized by active polyomavirus infection.
evidence.snippet: TSPyV DNA detection was significantly associated with disease (P<0.001), with 100% positivity of the lesional and 2% of the control samples.

evidence.reference_title: Trichodysplasia spinulosa is characterized by active polyomavirus infection.
evidence.snippet: TSPyV VP1 protein expression was detected only in lesional TS samples, restricted to the nuclei of inner root sheath cells over-expressing trichohyalin.

nodes.description: Itching accompanies the papular eruption in some patients.

evidence.reference_title: Trichodysplasia spinulosa in a renal transplant patient: A case report of successful treatment.
evidence.snippet: some slightly pruritic pink papules on the trunk and extremities.
